gaps.sentence: Your booking ___ (confirm) by email — check your spam folder.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + confirmed; the confirmation exists now.

gaps.sentence: She hates ___ (interrupt) when she's deep in work.
gaps.explanation: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like, avoid.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is said ___ in a private vault for decades.
gaps.explanation: 'For decades' before now: perfect passive infinitive to have been + kept.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ (resurface) at the time, so we took the coast route instead.
gaps.hint: in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: 'At the time' requires past continuous passive: was being + resurfaced.

gaps.sentence: He refuses ___ (tell) what to do by people he's never met.
gaps.explanation: 'Refuse' takes a to-infinitive; passive meaning needs to be + told.

gaps.sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
gaps.explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

gaps.sentence: The stolen car ___ (find) abandoned in a car park this morning.
gaps.explanation: 'This morning' (now over) takes past simple passive: was + found.

gaps.sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.
